about: Research sheet for the Massachusetts county edition. Every contact below was read on the date in reviewed_on from the page named beside it; scripts/make_county_state.py turns it into the edition files.
name: Massachusetts
phones_sentence: Massachusetts has no county veterans offices: every city and town has its own Veterans Service Officer. Each county card gives the state’s route to find yours.

offices.note: Veterans Service Officers help with state benefits, including Chapter 115, and referrals to federal VA help.
offices.selection: Massachusetts law puts a Veterans Service Officer in each of its 351 cities and towns, so no single office serves a county. Every county card shows the Executive Office of Veterans Services line and how to find the local VSO.

list.organization: Your city or town Veterans Service Officer (through the Executive Office of Veterans Services)
list.address: Executive Office of Veterans Services, One Bowdoin Square, 15 New Chardon Street, Suite 400, Boston, MA 02114
list.hours: Executive Office of Veterans Services: Monday to Friday, 8:45 a.m. to 5 p.m.
list.note: Massachusetts law puts a Veterans Service Officer in every city and town. Find yours with the state’s Find Your Local VSO search (by city, town or ZIP code), call your town hall and ask for Veterans’ Services, or call the Executive Office of Veterans Services and ask for your VSO. Chapter 115 benefits are applied for through your local VSO.

aging.source_title: Executive Office of Aging & Independence: Aging Support for Older Adults in Massachusetts
aging.source_scope: Call MassOptions at 1-800-243-4636 to get connected to local services; search excerpt. Massachusetts organizes aging services by city and town through Area Agencies on Aging and Aging Services Access Points; MassOptions refers callers to their local elder services agency (https://www.mass.gov/info-details/services; search excerpt). Every county shows the statewide line.
aging.description: MassOptions is Massachusetts’ free statewide line for older adults, people with disabilities and caregivers. It connects callers to their local Aging Services Access Point and Area Agency on Aging for home care, meals, caregiver support and options counseling.
aging.next_step_extra: Ask MassOptions for the elder services agency that serves your city or town.

regions.name: Massachusetts Long-Term Care Ombudsman Program
regions.source_title: Executive Office of Aging & Independence: Ombudsman Programs
regions.source_scope: Long-Term Care Ombudsman support is free for residents of nursing homes, rest homes and assisted living; call (617) 222-7495 to connect with your local ombudsman; search excerpt. Local programs are listed by city and town (https://www.mass.gov/info-details/find-an-ombudsman-representative-for-a-nursing-or-rest-home), so every county shows the state line.
notes: The state line connects you to the local ombudsman program for the facility’s city or town.

programs.name: Massachusetts veterans: your city or town Veterans Service Officer
programs.organization: Massachusetts Executive Office of Veterans Services
programs.description: Every Massachusetts city and town has a Veterans Service Officer, by state law. VSOs take applications for state benefits, including Chapter 115 financial help and the annuity program, make referrals and help with outreach and employment.
programs.next_step: Find your VSO with the state’s Find Your Local VSO search, or call your town hall and ask for Veterans’ Services. For help finding your VSO, call the Executive Office of Veterans Services at 617-210-5480 (Monday to Friday, 8:45 a.m. to 5 p.m.).
constraints: Chapter 115 benefits are means-tested; your VSO checks eligibility.

programs.name: MassOptions: Massachusetts’ aging and disability line
programs.organization: Executive Office of Aging & Independence, MassOptions
programs.description: MassOptions connects older adults, people with disabilities and caregivers to local services, including the Aging Services Access Point and Area Agency on Aging for their city or town. Military service is not required.
programs.next_step: Call MassOptions at 1-800-243-4636 and ask for the elder services agency for your city or town.
constraints: Each program has its own eligibility and waitlist.

sources.title: Executive Office of Aging & Independence: Aging Support for Older Adults in Massachusetts
sources.scope: To get connected to local services, call MassOptions at 1-800-243-4636; search excerpt.

sources.title: Mass.gov: Services for older adults
sources.scope: Ask MassOptions for your local elder services agency at 800-243-4636; search excerpt.

programs.name: Medicare counseling (SHINE) for Massachusetts
programs.organization: Executive Office of Aging & Independence, SHINE (Serving the Health Insurance Needs of Everyone)
programs.description: Free Medicare counseling from SHINE, Massachusetts’ State Health Insurance Assistance Program, with certified counselors around the state.
programs.next_step: Call SHINE through MassOptions at 1-800-243-4636 (TTY 800-439-2370), Monday to Friday, 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. For Medicare itself, call 800-MEDICARE (800-633-4227).
constraints: Have your Medicare card and drug list ready.

sources.title: Mass.gov: Get help paying Medicare costs
sources.scope: SHINE main line (800) 243-4636, Monday to Friday 9 to 5; TTY (800) 439-2370; search excerpt.

programs.name: Massachusetts Long-Term Care Ombudsman and elder abuse reporting
programs.organization: Executive Office of Aging & Independence: Long-Term Care Ombudsman Program; Adult Protective Services
programs.description: Free advocacy for residents of nursing homes, rest homes and assisted living. Adult Protective Services takes reports of abuse, neglect, exploitation or self-neglect of adults 60 and older, 24 hours a day.
programs.next_step: Call the ombudsman program at 617-222-7495. To report abuse of an adult 60 or older, call 800-922-2275 (24/7) or report online. In an emergency, call 911.
constraints: The ombudsman acts with the resident’s permission and is not a licensing agency.

sources.title: Mass.gov: Ombudsman Programs
sources.scope: Call (617) 222-7495 to connect with your local Long-Term Care Ombudsman; search excerpt.

sources.title: Mass.gov: Report Abuse of Adults Aged 60+
sources.scope: Reports 24 hours a day at (800) 922-2275 or online; search excerpt.

programs.name: Free legal help for older Massachusetts residents
programs.organization: Massachusetts Senior Legal Helpline (Volunteer Lawyers Project of Boston)
programs.description: The Massachusetts Senior Legal Helpline gives free legal information and referrals to residents 60 and older. Helpline advocates can check eligibility for a free attorney and help apply to a civil legal aid program.
programs.next_step: Age 60 and older: call the Senior Legal Helpline at 800-342-5297.
constraints: Most callers will not be eligible for a free attorney; the helpline can still advise and refer.

sources.title: Mass.gov: Learn more about elder law and find an attorney
sources.scope: Volunteer Lawyers Project; Massachusetts Senior Legal Helpline (800) 342-5297 for residents 60 and older; search excerpt.

sources.title: Mass.gov: The Massachusetts Senior Legal Helpline flyer
sources.scope: (800) 342-5297; most callers not eligible for a free attorney, advocates help apply; search excerpt.

programs.name: VA health care systems serving Massachusetts
programs.description: Massachusetts veterans are served by VA Boston Healthcare System (Jamaica Plain, West Roxbury and Brockton; 800-865-3384), the Edith Nourse Rogers Memorial Veterans Hospital in Bedford (781-687-2000) and the VA Central Western Massachusetts Healthcare System in Leeds (413-584-4040, toll-free 800-893-1522). Some southeastern communities are closer to the Providence VA Medical Center.
programs.next_step: Call the system nearest you, or use VA’s facility locator with your ZIP code. Not enrolled yet? Ask your local VSO for help applying.
constraints: Which system serves you depends on where you live; VA’s locator shows the right clinic.

coverage_scope: Referral edition. All 14 counties show how to reach the city or town Veterans Service Officer, the statewide MassOptions line for aging help, the long-term care ombudsman and at least one Center for Independent Living.
coverage_note: Veterans Service Officers are local to each city and town; the Executive Office of Veterans Services helps residents find theirs. Aging services are reached through MassOptions. Centers for Independent Living come from the ILRU national directory. Reviewed November 16, 2026. Contacts are not telephone-confirmed.
